node.title: Re^2: Greedy modifier found to be working non-greedy in a named group
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
the explanation of leftmost first and then longest will be valid even if I didn't use named groups. So, this behavior is generic.

Yes, [doc://perlre] says:

In Perl the groups are numbered sequentially regardless of being named or not. Thus in the pattern /(x)(?y)(z)/ $+{foo} will be the same as $2, and $3 will contain 'z'

And the description of (?|pattern) says:

Named captures are implemented as being aliases to numbered groups holding the captures

Also, I remember finding the description of the left-to-right operation of the regex engine in [http://shop.oreilly.com/product/9780596004927.do|the Camel] quite enlightening.
